newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan cult guru spent time in padded cell - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan cult guru spent time in padded cell - report.

text.p: The doomsday cult guru on trial for the Tokyo subway gas attack was taken to a padded cell last week after shouting and beating on the doors of his regular cell, media reports said on Thursday.

Shoko Asahara flew into a rage after returning from a court session last Friday in which he made confusing statements, first saying he took full responsibility for the subway gassing and then declaring his total innocence, the daily Asahi Shimbun said.

Officials at the Tokyo Detention Centre, where the leader of Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) is being held, refused to comment on the reports, which said the guru had since been returned to his regular cell.
It was unclear how long he spent in the padded cell.
The Asahi said Asahara, who is being tried for murder in the March 1995 subway nerve gas attack, which killed 11 people and harmed 6,000, told prison guards what sounded like: "I'm going mad".
Asahara, 41, also faces charges ranging from murder and attempted murder to illegal production of drugs and weapons. He could face execution by hanging if convicted of murder.

The media reports said Asahara became agitated after returning to his cell following a stormy court session last Friday. He started shouting at the top of his voice while repeatedly banging his fists against the walls and door of his cell. He was then taken to the padded cell so he would not hurt himself.
Prison officials refused to let court-appointed lawyers see Asahara for two days, on Monday and Tuesday, but he has since calmed down and is now back in his regular cell, the Asahi said.
"He's probably feigning insanity," the Asahi quoted an unidentified state prosecutor as saying. "Anyway, this will have no effect on the court schedule."
Asahara's next scheduled appearance at Tokyo District Court is on November 7.

On Friday, Asahara threw his murder trial into confusion with his outburst during questioning of a former cult disciple. "I would like to shoulder responsibility for all incidents. So please stop questioning him," Asahara said, only to declare after a court recess that he was "totally innocent".
